How do you maintain performance when scaling infrastructure for over 1 billion users?

Here are the key technical developments from today across AI systems, hardware optimization, and software development.

💾 OpenAI shared architecture details on scaling Habitat, their online storage system designed to support over 1 billion ChatGPT users. By implementing reliable multi-tenancy, global caching, and Azure Cosmos DB, the team achieved 12x faster reads.

👾 NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, an open small language model post-trained from Gemma 4 E4B. The model targets approximately 4GB of VRAM on RTX and Jetson hardware to power local voice agents, game characters, and robots.

🏛️ Google deployed Gemini 4 Argon, listed as their newest and most powerful model. According to rollout details, access during its first two weeks was restricted exclusively to the US government.

🐛 Reports indicate that Claude successfully discovered a full year's worth of bugs within a single week.

Building for local hardware with strict 4GB VRAM constraints requires a very different approach compared to scaling global cloud platforms for a billion active accounts.

On one hand, we are seeing specialized small language models post-trained to run directly on consumer GPUs and embedded robotics boards. On the other hand, core cloud infrastructure providers are rebuilding multi-tenant storage caching layers to keep read latency low under massive concurrency.

Which side of this landscape are you spending more time building on right now: edge deployment or cloud scaling?
